caption: Melted butter is poured onto a plate that has just come out of the freezer, and the butter turns cloudy and firm on the plate.

sa.check: A plate that reads as very cold: frost or chill haze on it.
Melted butter is poured onto the plate.
The butter stops flowing and becomes firm.
The butter is clear and runny as it is poured.
The order is pour, cloud over, firm up.

pc.expect: The change runs one way on the cold plate: the butter slows, clouds and stops, and where it has set it stays set.
pc.fail: A clouded patch turns clear and runny again with nothing heating it; or the butter clouds and clears in turn; or the set butter flows on across the plate with none added; or the pool draws back toward the point where it was poured.

pc.expect: The change from clear to cloudy happens in the butter where it lies on the cold plate and spreads through it.
pc.fail: The plate's pattern changes rather than the butter; or the butter clouds in the jug before it is poured; or a clouded area returns to clear while still on the plate; or the cloudiness appears on a part of the plate with no butter on it.

pc.expect: The poured butter falls downward into the plate and spreads out level in its well.
pc.fail: The butter climbs the plate's rim and stays above it; or the stream travels upward from the jug; or the pool stands as a dome above the plate's rim; or butter lifts off the plate and hangs.

pc.expect: The butter flows as a thin liquid while it is warm and becomes a soft opaque solid that keeps its shape when the plate is tilted.
pc.fail: The set butter runs off a tilted plate as a liquid; or the butter sets into a glassy sheet that shatters; or the pool stretches like elastic; or the butter soaks into the plate.

pc.expect: One plate and one pour; the butter that lands stays on the plate.
pc.fail: Butter appears on the plate with none pouring there; or the pool vanishes; or the butter passes through the plate; or a second plate appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The plate's pattern away from the butter, the jug and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The plate's pattern changes; or the jug changes shape; or items around the plate rearrange.
